records.text: A Hive'Ashi stinger is an airborne silithid of Hive'Ashi, one of the targets in the Cenarion war effort against the hive.
A Hive'Ashi worker is a silithid assigned to the worker role within Hive'Ashi. It is among the hive creatures targeted in the Cenarion war effort. In combat, it can cast a spell.
A Hive'Ashi defender is a silithid serving the defender role within Hive'Ashi. It is among the hive creatures targeted in the Cenarion war effort. In combat, it can cast Cripple.
A Hive'Ashi sandstalker is a silithid of Hive'Ashi targeted in the Cenarion war effort. It casts Sneak.
A Hive'Ashi swarmer is a silithid associated with Hive'Ashi, found across several areas in the zone.
A Hive'Zora waywatcher encountered in the hive grounds of Silithus. Commander Mar'alith's assault names waywatchers among its targets.
A Hive'Zora tunneler found in the hive grounds of Silithus. It attacks with a combat spell and is among the creatures targeted in Commander Mar'alith's assault.
A Hive'Zora wasp encountered in the hive grounds of Silithus. It uses poison in combat and is one of the hive creatures targeted by the assault from Cenarion Hold.
A Hive'Zora reaver in the hive grounds of Silithus, noted for knocking opponents down in combat. Commander Mar'alith's forces target reavers in their assault on the hive.
A Hive'Zora hive sister found in the hive grounds of Silithus. She attacks with toxic spit and is among the targets in Commander Mar'alith's assault.
A Hive'Regal ambusher is a silithid attacker associated with the Hive'Regal assault. It can cast Sneak.
A Hive'Regal burrower is one of the silithids targeted in the assault on Hive'Regal. It can cast an ability when wounded.
A Hive'Regal spitfire is an airborne silithid defending Hive'Regal. It attacks with Corrosive Acid Spit and is one of the targets in the assault on the hive.
A Hive'Regal slavemaker is a silithid encountered in the assault on Hive'Regal. It attacks with Volatile Infection and Poison Mind.
A Hive'Regal hive lord is a silithid encountered around Hive'Regal. It can charge a target when it becomes aggressive.
Stonelash Scorpids are common across several parts of Silithus. They are venomous attackers, using Venom Sting when fighting.
Stonelash Pincers are found across Silithus. In a fight, they use Tendon Rip to hinder their target.
Stonelash Flayers inhabit parts of Silithus and attack with Venom Sting.
Sand Skitterers range through several parts of Silithus. They attack with poison.
Rock Stalkers inhabit several parts of Silithus. Their recorded combat behavior includes using poison against their targets.

Dredge Strikers are desert worms found in Silithus. Windcaller Proudhorn reports that they ravaged a morrowgrain shipment bound for Cenarion Hold, threatening its supply caravans; they attack with Charge.
A large dredge beast in Silithus, the crusher is described as a southern cousin of the dredge strikers. Its presence threatens the supply lines around Cenarion Hold.
A dust stormer is one of the air elementals serving in the Crystal Vale. Duke Hydraxis identifies these elementals as enemies protecting objects of power there; this stormer uses lightning in combat.
A cyclone warrior is an air elemental in Silithus, distinguished among the stormers by its warrior title. It attacks with shock magic.

A desert rumbler is an earth elemental among the beings protecting objects of power in the Crystal Vale. Duke Hydraxis calls these elementals enemies of his people; the rumbler attacks with a crushing trample.
A desert rager is an earth elemental in Silithus, marked by its volatile name and an observed enraged display. It fights with earth shock.

Twilight Keeper Exeter is a lone Twilight’s Hammer cultist in Silithus. His keeper title and affiliation identify his place in the cult, while his combat training includes concussion blows and mortal strikes.
Twilight Keeper Havunth is a Twilight's Hammer member encountered in Silithus. In combat, he uses Fire Nova and Fire Blast.
Jarund Stoutstrider is associated with the Cenarion Circle.
A Twilight's Hammer combatant found at several Silithus locations, the Twilight Avenger fights with Enrage, triggered at low health and announced with an enraged yell.
A Twilight's Hammer geolord in Silithus, this combatant uses Boulder and Earth Shock. Huum Wildmane's account describes geolords as the heads of the cult's serpents and calls for striking them first.
A Twilight's Hammer Stonecaller found in Silithus, this combatant casts Fireball and also channels Nature while out of combat.
A Twilight's Hammer Master encountered in Silithus, this combatant uses Frostbolt in battle.
Shade of Ambermoon is a demon.
Zannok Hidepiercer sells leatherworking supplies in Silithus.

Layo Starstrike is a Cenarion Circle investigator at Valor's Rest in Silithus. He argues that neither Alliance nor Horde dead should remain trapped as tortured spirits, and seeks both to free Southwind's fallen and understand the silithid threat. An encrusted find prompts him to send it to the Circle's archivist for analysis.

Highlord Demitrian serves as the intermediary in Thunderaan's release, directing the search for the materials needed to free the Windseeker. After Thunderaan is defeated, Demitrian is made to use those materials to awaken Thunderfury; faced with the dormant blade, he cowers and begs to be spared. The quest account calls him a betrayer, though these records give little detail about his earlier part in the betrayal.
The Windreaver is an elemental whose invasion brings forces into northwestern Silithus. His presence is marked by gales and howling winds carrying the sound of his fury.
A whirling elemental invader whose combat attacks include Whirlwind.
Setis uses War Stomp and Crowd Pummel in combat.
Gretheer is a beast whose combat repertoire includes Deadly Poison and Web.
Lapress is a beast whose combat attacks include Rend.
Zora is a creature that casts Poison Bolt when a target is within 30 yards.
Rex Ashil is a creature that casts Pierce Armor when a target is within 5 yards.
Krellack is a creature that casts Fatal Sting when a target is within 5 yards.
Grubthor is a creature that casts Trample when a target is within 5 yards.
Huricanian is a creature that casts Chain Lightning in combat.
Twilight Lord Everun is a creature associated with the Twilight's Hammer. In combat, he casts Fireball and Shadow Shock at targets within 20 yards.
Nelson the Nice is a gnome who says he visits Silithus each year around this time, jokes about his bunions, and invites a companion to stroll with him.

Ralo'shan the Eternal Watcher remembers the Qiraji devastation that began in this desert nearly a thousand years ago, when thousands died. He says he is one of the few who remain, chained to past and present; though he does not know why he must stay stationed there, he believes he must.

At Bronzebeard's Encampment, Rutgar Glyphshaper works with others to investigate the strange glyphs on crystals found in the silithid hives. He considers the markings unfamiliar and hopes Frankal's research will explain them. After the rubbings help recreate the glyphs on a prism, Rutgar sends it to Geologist Larksbane for further study.

At Bronzebeard's Encampment in Silithus, Frankal Stonebridge is investigating silithid and Qiraji language as part of work begun by Rutgar. He seeks brains from each of the three silithid types to formulate an elixir that could make their glyphs easier to decipher. He also takes part in questioning the dwarves about Mistress Natalia Mar’alith; his reply to a returned task shows little patience, telling the player he has no time for it.
Glibb is Brann Bronzebeard's pet monkey at Bronzebeard's Encampment in Silithus.

Calandrath is the innkeeper at Cenarion Hold and a cook trying to adapt to desert life. She misses Auberdine's birds and trees, experiments with desert herbs, and wants to make bitter sandworm meat palatable. She seeks help preparing smoked desert dumplings and can identify the unfamiliar herbs and spices in a recipe.
Khur Hornstriker supplies Cenarion Hold with spellcasting relics and alchemical reagents.
Vargus is Cenarion Hold’s blacksmith. He repairs armor and weapons and exchanges Cenarion campaign badges for battlegear as members earn the Circle’s trust.
Cloud Skydancer is a hippogryph master at Cenarion Hold, offering travelers flight routes from the outpost.
Runk Windtamer is a wind rider master at Cenarion Hold, offering travelers flight routes from the outpost.
Mishta is a trade-supplies merchant who offers goods for browsing. She is running dangerously low on supplies and impatiently wonders why the goblin responsible for bringing more is taking so long.

Baristolth is a Watcher bound to the service of the Bronze master after being rescued from death, and he has kept that charge for a thousand years. As the Qiraji prepare for war again, he seeks the master's return and works to identify a champion worthy of the Brood of Nozdormu's trust. He regards that champion's duties as demanding enough to require deputizing others for help.

Commander Mar'alith commands the Cenarion Hold outpost in Silithus, but his duty there keeps him from searching personally for his missing wife, Natalia. She vanished while researching near Bronzebeard's camp after weeks of troubling behavior, including speaking to herself. He sends others to learn what happened and find her, torn between hope and the possibility that she must be stopped. Her fate leaves him shaken and struggling to understand C'Thun's role.

Vish Kozus is Captain of the Guard at Cenarion Hold. He manages practical needs for the mounted guard, including boots and grinding stones, and handles reports of threats to patrols and expeditions. He offers rewards for dealing with dangers such as Deathclasp, whose removal opens a strategic route through the southern mountains.

Geologist Larksbane studies Silithus through its relics and the Qiraji. She gathers fragments of a Twilight's Hammer tablet, seeks help deciphering it, and investigates glyphs that may summon a Qiraji emissary to obtain a crystal key. Her account of the Qiraji prophecy traces the war against Staghelm's night elf forces and the fall of Southwind; the prophecy's threat leaves her pale and fearful for the future.
Cenarion Hold Infantry serve as guards at the hold. When combat begins, they challenge those spilling blood on neutral ground and threaten or rebuke the offenders.
A Silithus dragonkin of the Brood of Nozdormu.

Beetix Ficklespragg is an alchemist at Cenarion Hold who is trying to save her cousin Noggle after he returns from gathering herbs with a strong poison in his veins. She slows the venom, then seeks samples from likely scorpids and other poisonous creatures when her first antidote fails. Her anxious encouragement and relief as he recovers show how personally she takes the effort.

Noggle Ficklespragg gathers rare herbs and reagents for Cenarion Hold alchemists. After Deathclasp drives him into a nest of stonelash flayers, he is poisoned, weak and disoriented; his cousin Beetix works to cure him. While recovering, he worries that losing his satchel has deprived them of reagents needed for the Hold’s potions, and is grateful when it is returned.

Windcaller Proudhorn welcomes recruits to Cenarion Hold and directs its effort against the silithid. He regards the Hold as strategically vital, but warns that desert worms threaten its supply caravans; he organizes the defense of those routes and calls for the dredge strikers and crushers to be thinned before supplies are jeopardized.

Hermit Ortell is a deserter from the Twilight’s Hammer, whose members still hunt him. He wants to decipher a tablet using the sect’s three-part Twilight Lexicon, then studies its encoded monthly bulletin for news of the search and information he can share. He treats enemies of the Twilight’s Hammer as potential allies, though his guarded greeting warns strangers away.

Deathclasp is a giant female scorpid considered a threat to patrols and expeditions in southern Silithus. She is believed to have retreated to the southern mountain range amid increased silithid activity, and attacks with paralyzing poison and powerful blows.
Mayna is a named Twilight Keeper of the Twilight's Hammer in Silithus. In combat, she uses Mind Flay and Shadow Word: Pain.
Twilight Flamereavers are humanoid spellcasters found at multiple sites in Silithus, where they use Immolate in combat.
Vyral the Vile is identified as the local leader of the Twilight's Hammer cult at Twilight's Run, a cave in northeast Silithus. He uses Fireball and Shadow Shock in combat.
Twilight Overlords are humanoid figures bearing the Twilight's Hammer name, found at multiple sites in Silithus. They use Frostbolt in combat.

Once Mar’alith’s beloved wife, Natalia disappeared after weeks of strange behavior and continued research. Now a hostile servant of C’Thun, she threatens sacrifice and declares that the old god will reclaim the world. Her words show how far she has turned from the life her husband remembers.

Huum Wildmane directs Cenarion Hold’s campaign against the Twilight’s Hammer in Silithus. He identifies its camps and geolords as immediate threats, then sends the player after Vyral the Vile at Twilight’s Run and asks for his signet ring. His work also advances the effort against the Abyssal Council, whose influence over the cult’s operations has emerged through the arcane wind stones.

Aurel Goldleaf is a Cenarion Hold craftsman aiding the campaign against the Abyssal Council. He makes Twilight Hammer disguises, including a medallion of station and a ring of lordship, so allies can approach wind stones and ambush the summoned council members.
Aendel Windspear is a ghostly woman in Cenarion Hold. She regards visitors with mistrust and remains silent.

Bor Wildmane and his older brother Huum keep watch on the Twilight's Hammer in Silithus while others focus on the silithid. Bor works to disrupt the cult's communications and its chain of command, asking for encrypted texts and proof of victories over abyssal forces. He values evidence of success and warns that fighting an Abyssal Lord calls for a capable force.
Kania is an enchanting supplies vendor in Silithus, offering goods to visitors who want to browse her stock.

Captain Blackanvil serves as an Ironforge Brigade captain and handles field duty papers. He treats a skirmish as modest proof of field duty, then directs the bearer to take the papers to Cenarion Hold.
An Ironforge Brigade rifleman, equipped to engage enemies at range as one of the brigade’s soldiers.
An Ironforge Brigade footman serving among the brigade’s soldiers, with a frontline infantry role.

Janela Stouthammer handles field supplies for the Ironforge Brigade at its Silithus outpost, receiving armor kits and weapons. She says the kits will go to the soldiers and jokes that sharper blades should quiet complaints. The brigade watches Hive’Zora as the Cenarion Circle druids anticipate major silithid activity.

Arcanist Nozzlespring handles a specialized supply request for the Ironforge Brigade near Hive’Zora, receiving volatile components including oil, rocket fuel, and blasting powder. Nozzlespring says the materials will come in handy, though the request gives no further detail about their intended use.

Windcaller Yessendra is a druid who helps the Cenarion Circle’s campaign against the Qiraji by working with recovered Qiraji materials. She explains that their rings can be refitted with purer gems, and offers to make powerful rings from them. Her account of the war also recognizes the traders and craftsmen whose supplies support the fighting.

Warden Haro says he came to Silithus to aid his fellow druids when the war began and chose to remain after the Gates of Ahn’Qiraj opened, because he believes more work remains. He is a weapon craftsman, eager to practice his craft on Qiraji materials; he describes making powerful weapons from them for those who prove their allegiance to the Cenarion Circle. His words join practical craftsmanship to the Circle’s continuing fight.

Keyl Swiftclaw is a Cenarion Circle ally in Silithus who offers to turn Qiraji drapes, idols, and scarabs into protective cloaks for those aiding the assault on Ahn'Qiraj. He speaks confidently of the Qiraji threat and promises his work will help against it.

Windcaller Kaldon is a Cenarion Circle war coordinator at Cenarion Hold. He sends volunteers to perform field duty with either the Alliance's Ironforge Brigade or the Horde's Orgrimmar Legion, then prepares further assignments. He recognizes the tension between those forces and asks volunteers to keep their distance from the opposing camp; he hopes their combined effort will defeat the Qiraji.
Morna leads the Twilight's Hammer marauders, mounted cultists who prey on Cenarion patrols and caravans. She is a terrible warrior who uses Mortal Strike, Sunder Armor and Piercing Howl.
A Twilight's Hammer marauder, one of the mounted cultists targeting Cenarion patrols and caravans. This fighter charges when drawing an enemy's attention and can become enraged.
A Cenarion Outrider.
Elder Primestone speaks of the new year, the bright moon and the awakening of the ancients. The elder frames this observance as a way to honor the old races and offers a reflective blessing.
Elder Bladesing speaks in terms of stars changing course and offering hope and strength for ages to come. The elder presents the night sky as a source of answers to earthly mysteries.

Cenarion Scout Landion has spent days watching silithid movements inside Hive'Regal for the Cenarion effort to gather intelligence. He says close observation takes practice and warns against trying it when avoidable. His role calls for a written report to help the Cenarion forces act on what he learns.

Cenarion Scout Azenel has watched silithid movements inside Hive'Zora for days as part of the Cenarion intelligence effort. She would rather not spend her days in a silithid-filled tunnel, but accepts the danger as worthwhile if it helps win the war, and says she will continue as long as needed. Her work is to provide a written report.

Cenarion Scout Jalia has spent days watching silithid movements inside Hive'Ashi for the Cenarion intelligence effort. She believes the silithids pose a greater danger than most have seen firsthand and warns that darker powers are behind their activity. Her warning points to a wider threat, though she does not identify those powers here.

Krug Skullsplit is an Orgrimmar Legion captain who says he and his people serve Thrall with pride and will travel as far as needed to defeat the enemy. He handles Field Duty Papers for the campaign; his response treats the reported skirmish as modest field duty and sends the papers back to Cenarion Hold with a dry remark about the cushy work awaiting there.
Merok Longstride handles supply requests for the Orgrimmar Legion near Hive’Regal in Silithus. He asks for weapons and armor kits, and says he will distribute the kits to the troops.
J.D. Shadesong is a quest giver.
Shadow Priestess Shai is a troll serving the Orgrimmar Legion in Silithus. She handles its request for unusual ingredients and plans to make a concoction to use against the silithid.
An Orgrimmar Legion grunt found in Silithus.

Jonathan the Revelator identifies himself as keeper of the sacred gong and watcher of the Bronze Flight, empowered by the Timeless One. He offers a choice from the timeless treasure trove as aid in battles against C’Thun.
Squire Leoren Mal'derath is the stable master of Cenarion Hold, where he greets visitors and identifies himself as Leoren.

Colossus Researcher Sophia seeks samples from the Colossus of Zora for research that Lord Maxwell Tyrosus believes could help the war against the Scourge. Her servants were nearly killed recovering a sample, and she urges haste in getting it to him at Light's Hope Chapel.

Colossus Researcher Nestor seeks a fresh sample from the fallen Colossus of Ashi for delivery to Oglethorpe Obnoticus in Booty Bay. He offers a sample already collected and stresses that it must be delivered before it spoils.

Colossus Researcher Eazel is collecting samples from the fallen Colossus of Regal. He wants a sample delivered quickly to Overseer Oilfist at Thorium Point, and expresses contempt for Oilfist while emphasizing the generous payment.
Sergeant Carnes is a military officer who jokes bitterly that his promotion has left him stationed outside a Silithus bughive with sweaty dwarves. He sarcastically thanks the Captain for the posting.

Dirk Thunderwood is a Ravenholdt operative pursuing a potent poison compound for Lord Ravenholdt with his brother, who also runs poison operations. He seeks venom sacs from Kurinnaxx and Venoxis and warns that the job calls for friends.
Garon Hutchins is a guarded figure who tells visitors to leave off, saying he has nothing for them.
Chief Expeditionary Requisitioner Enkles is identified by name as a requisitioner with the expeditionary force.
Apothecary Quinard is identified by name as an apothecary.
A Cenarion scout, identified by role with the Cenarion presence at Cenarion Hold.
General Kirika leads the Horde effort to secure Silithyst as Alliance competition for Silithus's resources grows. She calls for more hands and warns of the desert's dangers and the Alliance presence.

Marshal Bluewall leads from the Alliance encampment near Hive'Zora as the faction scrambles to catch up with Horde Silithyst gathering. He urges recruits into the desert quickly, pressed by casualties, scarce reinforcements and the need to keep the resource from Horde hands.

Scout Bloodfist is a Horde scout near Hive'Regal who directs new recruits to General Kirika, leaving their training to her. His impatient welcome reflects the strain of desert fighting and the dwarves' steady reinforcements.
Rifleman Torrig greets new arrivals with a mordant warning that good soldiers are dying in the desert, then sends them to Marshal Bluewall. His words carry the urgency of the Silithus fighting.
An Alliance Silithyst Sentinel is a veteran combatant in the Silithus resource conflict. It uses Mortal Strike when it enters combat.
A Horde Silithyst Sentinel is a veteran combatant in the Silithus resource conflict. It uses Mortal Strike when it enters combat.

npcs.name: Silithus Dust Turnin Quest Doodad Horde

records.text: A Horde Silithyst extractor tied to the struggle over Silithus's crystal resources. The campaign description frames the effort as a race with the Alliance to secure the desert's resources.

An Alliance-aligned Silithus Flame Warden associated with the Midsummer festival. Its greeting urges honoring Alliance fires across Alliance settlements and desecrating Horde fires, reflecting the event's faction rivalry.

A Horde-aligned Silithus Flame Keeper associated with the Midsummer festival. Its greeting urges honoring Horde fires across Horde settlements and desecrating Alliance fires, reflecting the event's faction rivalry.

place_records.text: You are in Silithus, a desert in Kalimdor that neither the Alliance nor the Horde holds. Cenarion Hold is its one main settlement, and it belongs to neither side. Silithid hives fill the wastes, and Twilight camps and stonelash scorpids roam the sands. The Alliance and the Horde race to take the crystal silithyst from the desert. Twilight's Hammer still hunts Hermit Ortell, a deserter who hides in Silithus.

You are in The Scarab Wall, a silithid site in Silithus with a spirit healer for the dead. Stonelash flayers and a creature named Setis prowl the sands. A crystal here shows the past to whoever looks into it.

You are in Southwind Village, a ruin in Silithus that was once a night elf base. Silithid hives have overrun it, and the tortured spirits of its druids and sentinels still wander the ruins. Stonelash pincers and dredge strikers roam among them.
You are in Twilight Base Camp, a Twilight camp in Silithus. Twilight geolords, avengers and stonecallers hold it, and a Twilight Keeper named Havunth is among them.
You are in The Crystal Vale, a stretch of Silithus desert where desert rumblers and dust stormers roam. Huricanians are seen here too.

You are in The Scarab Dais, where Jonathan the Revelator keeps the sacred gong and watches over the Bronze Flight, empowered by the Timeless One. He offers aid against C'Thun drawn from a timeless trove.

You are in Hive'Ashi, a silithid hive in Silithus. Hive'Ashi swarmers and defenders fill it. Cenarion Scout Jalia has spent days watching the silithids inside for the Cenarion intelligence effort, and she believes darker powers are behind their activity.

You are in Hive'Zora, a silithid hive in Silithus where the Alliance has camped. The Ironforge Brigade keeps an encampment here, and Marshal Bluewall urges recruits into the desert to gather silithyst. Hive'Zora wasps and reavers fill the tunnels, and Cenarion scouts watch the silithids from within.

You are in Hive'Regal, a silithid hive in Silithus where the Orgrimmar Legion holds ground. Orgrimmar Legion captain Krug Skullsplit is here, and Merok Longstride handles its supply requests. Hive'Regal slavemakers, spitfires and hive lords roam the tunnels, and a spirit healer serves the dead.

You are in Valor's Rest, a graveyard in Silithus where Cenarion Circle investigator Layo Starstrike works. He argues that the dead of both sides should not stay trapped as tortured spirits. Zannok Hidepiercer sells leatherworking supplies here.
You are in The Swarming Pillar, a silithid site in Silithus. Hive'Ashi swarmers and stingers are found here.
You are in Twilight Post, a Twilight camp in Silithus. Twilight geolords, avengers and stonecallers are posted here, along with a Twilight Keeper named Mayna.
You are in Twilight Outpost, a Twilight camp in Silithus. Twilight masters and a Twilight Lord named Everun hold it with stonecallers, avengers and geolords.

You are in Ravaged Twilight Camp, a camp in Silithus. Highlord Demitrian is here, and he is searching for the materials needed to free Thunderaan the Windseeker from his prison. Desert rumblers prowl the ground around the camp.
You are in Bones of Grakkarond, a place in Silithus. Dredge crushers, stonelash pincers, cyclone warriors and desert rumblers are the dangers here.

You are in Cenarion Hold, an outpost in Silithus that neither the Alliance nor the Horde holds. Its inn, smithy and flight master are here, and Windcaller Proudhorn organizes the defense of its supply routes against desert worms and silithid. Huum Wildmane directs the campaign against the Twilight's Hammer, and Commander Mar'alith cannot leave his post to search personally for his missing wife, Natalia.

You are in Staghelm Point, a place in Silithus where Twilight overlords, flamereavers, avengers and masters, stonelash scorpids and dredge strikers are the dangers. Ralo'shan the Eternal Watcher stays stationed here, remembering the Qiraji devastation of nearly a thousand years ago, and he says he does not know why he must stay.

You are in Bronzebeard Encampment, an encampment in Silithus where Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge are studying the glyphs on crystals from the silithid hives. Frankal wants brains from each silithid type to make an elixir for deciphering those glyphs, and rock stalkers are the danger here. Glibb, Brann Bronzebeard's pet monkey, is here too.
